title: 2026-10-22_Sednit_Xagent_Investigation_3d1
description: Investigate a compromised network where the Sednit group's Xagent malware has been detected. Identify the malware's presence, understand its behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The Sednit group, also known as APT29, is a sophisticated cyber espionage group believed to be operating out of Russia. They are known for targeting government agencies, diplomatic institutions, and research organizations. Their primary malware, Xagent, is a backdoor used for espionage purposes.

In this scenario, you will investigate a compromised network where the Sednit group's Xagent malware has been detected. Your goal is to identify the malware's presence, understand its behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: target
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the target host:
- Hostname: target
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running.
levels.solution:
To identify the suspicious service, you can use the following command:

`systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`

The service name is lg3.exe.service. This is the final flag.

hints.title: Check running services for suspicious activity
hints.content: Check the running services and their associated processes.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you've identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after reboot. This will help you understand the malware's persistence mechanism.
levels.solution:
To determine the persistence mechanism, you can use the following command:

`systemctl list-timers`

The persistence identifier is lab-checkin.timer. This is the final flag.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control (C2) server. Determine which network port is used for this communication.
levels.solution:
To determine the network port used for C2 communication, you can use the following command:

`ss -tulnp`

The C2 port number is 4444. This is the final flag.

hints.title: Investigate network connections for C2 communication
hints.content: Investigate the service configuration and network connections.
